description: Comprehensive reasoning vault for Cartesian coordinate system, plotting points, quadrants, intercepts, horizontal and vertical lines, slope calculation, slope-intercept form, parallel and perpendicular slopes, and coordinate modeling.

archetypes.name: Cartesian Coordinate Plane and Point Identification
archetypes.coreConcept: Locate ordered pairs (x, y) relative to origin and determine coordinate quadrants based on signs of abscissa and ordinate.
archetypes.mentalModel: Two orthogonal number lines intersecting at origin (0, 0).

archetypes.name: Finding X- and Y-Intercepts of Linear Graphs
archetypes.coreConcept: Determine where a line crosses coordinate axes by setting y = 0 for x-intercept and x = 0 for y-intercept.
archetypes.mentalModel: Boundary collision points of a linear trajectory with coordinate axes.

archetypes.name: Equations of Horizontal and Vertical Lines
archetypes.coreConcept: Horizontal lines have equation y = c and zero slope; vertical lines have equation x = c and undefined slope.
archetypes.mentalModel: Fixed altitude trajectories versus plumb line vertical fences.
archetypes.governingRelation: y = c \implies m = 0 \land x = c \implies m \text{ undefined}

archetypes.name: Calculating Slope from Two Coordinate Points
archetypes.coreConcept: Slope measures rate of vertical change per unit horizontal change: m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1).
archetypes.mentalModel: Steepness ratio of vertical rise to horizontal run.

archetypes.name: Slope-Intercept Form y = mx + b
archetypes.coreConcept: Identify rate of change m and initial baseline offset b from linear equation y = mx + b.
archetypes.mentalModel: Starting elevation plus continuous steady-state climb rate.

archetypes.name: Parallel Lines and Slope Equality Invariant
archetypes.coreConcept: Two non-vertical lines are parallel if and only if they have equal slopes: m1 = m2. L3 problem form: show a worked solution that makes the mistake 'parallel negative reciprocal (tag `c14-parallel-negative-reciprocal-trap`)'; the prompt shows the work as 'Line N: $...$' lines and the learner picks the first wrong line (answerSpec `choice` with `verify.flaw`; asking for the corrected value lets the learner just recompute, 06 §2.3).
archetypes.mentalModel: Equidistant trajectories maintaining constant separation indefinitely.

archetypes.name: Midpoint Coordinates of Line Segments
archetypes.coreConcept: The midpoint coordinate is the arithmetic mean of endpoint coordinates: ((x1 + x2)/2, (y1 + y2)/2). L3 problem form: show a worked solution that makes the mistake 'subtract coordinates for midpoint (tag `c14-subtract-coordinates-for-midpoint-trap`)'; the prompt shows the work as 'Line N: $...$' lines and the learner picks the first wrong line (answerSpec `choice` with `verify.flaw`; asking for the corrected value lets the learner just recompute, 06 §2.3).
archetypes.mentalModel: Equilibrium center of mass of two coordinate endpoints.

archetypes.name: Perpendicular Lines and Orthogonal Slopes
archetypes.coreConcept: Two non-vertical lines are perpendicular if and only if their slopes multiply to -1: m1 * m2 = -1. L3 problem form: show a worked solution that makes the mistake 'forgot negative sign inversion (tag `c14-forgot-negative-sign-inversion-trap`)'; the prompt shows the work as 'Line N: $...$' lines and the learner picks the first wrong line (answerSpec `choice` with `verify.flaw`; asking for the corrected value lets the learner just recompute, 06 §2.3).
archetypes.mentalModel: Quarter-turn rotation (90 degrees) flipping and inverting rise and run.

archetypes.name: Two-Vendor Linear Cost Break-Even Modeling
archetypes.coreConcept: Each of two vendors is described by two (quantity, cost) points. Build each line (slope = marginal cost, intercept = fixed cost), find their intersection (the break-even quantity), and use it to choose the cheaper vendor for a given order size.
archetypes.mentalModel: Two empirical lines; their intersection splits the decision space.
archetypes.governingRelation: m_i = \frac{\Delta C_i}{\Delta x},\ b_i = C_i - m_i x_i,\quad m_1 x + b_1 = m_2 x + b_2

archetypes.name: Unknown Vertex from a Target Triangle Area
archetypes.coreConcept: Two vertices of a triangle are fixed on the coordinate grid and the third lies on a given horizontal or vertical line. The area is given. The base length and the distance to the line give an absolute-value equation for the unknown coordinate, which has two solutions; both must be reported (or the one that satisfies an extra condition).
archetypes.mentalModel: Area target -> height -> absolute-value equation with two cases.
